edges.prerequisite: Control Plane Approaches: Per-Router vs. SDN
edges.rationale: The overview establishes the per-router control paradigm in which routing algorithms run inside each router; OSPF is presented as an intra-AS instance of that approach, so the framing is needed to situate it.
OSPF implements link-state routing within an autonomous system, so understanding Dijkstra's least-cost computation and complete-topology link-state dissemination is a direct prerequisite.

edges.prerequisite: Control Plane Approaches: Per-Router vs. SDN
edges.rationale: BGP is another instance of the distributed per-router control paradigm; the overview's taxonomy of per-router vs. SDN control provides the conceptual frame for why BGP computes and advertises routes among routers/ASes rather than via a central controller.

Inter-AS routing presupposes the notion of autonomous systems with their own internal routing; BGP interconnects ASes whose intra-AS routing (e.g., OSPF) must be understood first to see how interior and exterior routes compose.

BGP is a path-vector protocol that generalizes the distance-vector mechanism of iteratively exchanging reachability vectors with neighbors; the DV algorithm's distributed, iterative mechanics prepare students for BGP's AS-path advertisements.

edges.prerequisite: Control Plane Approaches: Per-Router vs. SDN
edges.dependent: SDN Control Plane: Controller and Applications
edges.rationale: The SDN control plane topic elaborates the SDN approach defined in the overview; its controller/application architecture and separation of data and control planes presuppose familiarity with the SDN paradigm introduced there.
